top.h1: How big was the woolly mammoth?
top.answer: A full-grown Siberian woolly mammoth bull stood about 2.7 to 2.9 m (9 ft) at the shoulder and weighed about 4 to 5 tonnes. Bigger European bulls reached about 3 to 3.3 m (10 to 11 ft) and about 5 to 7 tonnes. Ours is one real Siberian bull found frozen in 1900: 2.71 m (8.9 ft) at the shoulder, about 4.2 tonnes, reconstructed from his bones. Beside the person of 1.70 m, his shoulder is about one and a half people high.
top.answer_more: So a Siberian mammoth bull was about as tall as an Asian elephant bull, and a little heavier for his height. A big African bush elephant bull stands about half a metre taller and weighs more.

scale.what: Our woolly mammoth beside a person 1.70 m tall, to one scale. He is built to the size and frame of one real animal, the Berezovka bull, found frozen in north-east Siberia in 1900. The mark at his shoulder is his own height in the flesh, 271 cm (8.9 ft), reconstructed from his bones. When he died he had one tusk left, the left. The right had fallen out long before, and the hunters who found him cut off the left and sold it. Ours carries both, the right as a mirror of the left, a reconstruction.

guess.q: How old was the Berezovka bull when he died?
guess.a: About 45 to 50 years, by the museum that holds him. He was a full-grown bull, so his size is an adult's, not a young animal's.

paras: The woolly mammoth, Mammuthus primigenius, was a close relative of today's elephants, and not their ancestor. A typical Siberian bull was about the height of an Asian elephant bull and a little heavier for that height. Its pelvis was broader and its upper leg bones longer. An African bush elephant bull, the biggest land animal alive, stands up to about half a metre taller and weighs about 5 to 7 tonnes. The big European mammoth bulls matched it. Unlike any elephant, the mammoth had a thick coat, small ears and a short tail.

Three tiers: long dark outer hairs, a lighter middle tier and a pale underwool. In life the coat was probably dark brown and not one flat colour. The ginger of museum hair is a burial colour: in frozen ground hair loses its own colour and takes up the soil's. Our bull's longest hair, on the chin and chest, was about 50 cm, by the estimate of the leader of the dig.

They curved out and down, then up and in, like a loose spiral, and were worn on the outer side of the tip. Old bulls' tusks reached up to 4 m and about 100 kg, by the museum that holds our bull. Cows' were smaller and nearly straight, about 2 to 2.2 m.

The trunk ended in a long upper finger and a short lower lobe, as frozen trunks show. Lower down it widened between two skin folds, which no living elephant has, for a purpose still debated. The ears were small, about 30 cm high on a frozen bull. The tail was short, on our bull 36 cm, with a tuft of long hair.

The top of the head was the highest point. Behind it a dip, then a hump over the shoulders on the tall spines of the back bones, then a back sloping to low hips. Old bulls showed a waist between hump and head.

In August 1900 a local hunter found him in the bank of the Berezovka River, a tributary of the Kolyma in north-east Siberia. In 1901 an expedition from St Petersburg under Otto Herz dug him out, and in 1902 he reached the city. Since 1903 he has been on show in the Zoological Museum there. The skeleton is mounted. The body is restored in the pose he was found in, on his belly with the front legs forward, the head and trunk modelled. He was far from complete: the top of the head and much of the back had thawed and been eaten long before, and most of the trunk was gone. He had grass between his teeth. He most likely fell into a gully or off a bank, broke his pelvis and a front leg and could not get out. Seeds on the plants he had eaten point to late summer.

points: The lengths of his long bones and the breadth of his pelvis, and from them his height and weight.
The width of his skull and jaw.
His tail, 36 cm, and his skin, 19 to 23 mm thick.
His hair on the legs, chin and chest.
The weight of his one tusk, about 29 kg.
Head, ear, eye and forefoot: after another frozen Siberian bull.
The side outline: after Larramendi's restoration of a third bull, 2016.
The trunk: after other frozen mammoths.
The shape of every bone: after other mounts. Only the lengths and widths are his.
The right tusk: a mirror of the left.

end: So our mammoth is one animal in its size and frame, and several in its form.

blocks.nav: When did woolly mammoths go extinct?
blocks.h: When did woolly mammoths go extinct?
paras: Woolly mammoths lived for hundreds of thousands of years, in the last ice age from Spain to Alaska, and they died out in steps, not all at once. On the mainland the last ones lived in northern Siberia until about 10,000 years ago, on St Paul Island off Alaska until about 5,600 years ago. The last known population lived on Wrangel Island, in the Arctic Ocean off Siberia, until about 4,000 years ago, and they were not dwarfs. Why they died out is argued: on the mainland the warming at the end of the ice age and hunting by people, in shares nobody has settled. On St Paul the island shrank and fresh water ran short, with no people there. On Wrangel the end seems to have come fast, and nobody knows why: an icing from rain on snow is one idea, and people cannot be ruled out.
Two things decide every number on this page.

points: Where the heights and weights come from:

one study of 2016 brought together the measurements of many mammoth and elephant skeletons and did the calculations the same way for all. The height is the skeleton's plus about 5.5 percent for flesh, the weight the volume of a body drawn around the bones. We found nothing newer.
Ours is one animal, not the species:
one Siberian bull, a little under the Siberian average. So three numbers stand apart here: our bull, the typical Siberian bull and the big European bulls.

blocks.intro: For each number: where it came from, and what it means.

rows.text: A handbook figure of 2007 for a large bull, spread by a widely used size chart. It fits a large European bull, not a typical Siberian one, and not ours.
Maxima from the museum in St Petersburg. Bulls up to 3.5 m, old bulls' tusks up to 4 m and about 100 kg, not averages.
On the common size chart the 4 m animal is the southern mammoth, another species. Even record European woolly mammoth bulls stayed under 4 m.
6 tonnes is the average of the big European bulls, and of African bush elephant bulls. Only the very largest reached 8 tonnes, such as a bull from Siegsdorf in Bavaria at about 8.2 tonnes.
The colour of hair that lay thousands of years in frozen ground, losing its own pigment and taking up the soil's. In life the coat was probably dark brown and mixed.

rows.term: A skirt of hair 80 to 90 cm long
rows.text: The museum that holds our bull gives this figure, and 70 to 80 cm elsewhere on the same page. On our bull the dig found torn bunches of hair 36 cm long. Whole, they would have been about 50 cm, by the estimate of the dig's leader.
Roughly true, and only of the last known population, on Wrangel Island, about 4,000 years ago. On the mainland the last ones lived until about 10,000 years ago.

rows.term: Frozen with food in the mouth
rows.text: Our bull had grass between his teeth. From that grew the picture of a mammoth frozen on the spot while eating. The leader of the dig read the find as a fall, with broken bones and a short death struggle.

blocks.nav: Why our woolly mammoth looks like this
blocks.h: Why our woolly mammoth looks like this
paras: It is built to the measurements of the Berezovka bull's bones and stands in a walking stride, the trunk's tip on the ground.

items.a: Yes. The museum in St Petersburg names several more. Among them: the Adams mammoth of 1799, the first full skeleton science had, and the Taymyr mammoth of 1948 with muscle, skin and hair. Frozen bodies are why the trunk, ears and coat of this species are known at all.

items.q: How long ago did the Berezovka bull live?
items.a: About 44,000 years, by the radiocarbon date of the museum that holds him. The frozen ground kept his skin, his hair and the grass between his teeth all that time.
